text: The Marisol Trench probe reached 6,100 metres before investigators halted the descent, according to a technical log released Thursday by the Hesperian Oceanic Authority and reviewed by The Continental Record. The agency said the vehicle, Aster-4, completed its deepest pass at 03:18 local time on 14 October, measuring pressure and temperature gradients in the trench’s central chute. Chief engineer Liora Venn said in a written statement that the probe remained stable throughout the final 200 metres but was ordered back after a telemetry fault appeared in its ascent beacon. The authority said no hull breach occurred and that the data set would be published next week.
